items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then Antoinette Handy, bless her heart, saw that it could be made a lot more visible and a lot more exciting were it connected to an event.

ctx.x: Right. That’s why I thought it might be nice if you said – spoke about it a little bit.

But I thought – first of all, it started out with very little fanfare. It was just like the [NEA] folk music awards, in that they simply gave the award – $20,000 – and that was the end of it. Then Antoinette Handy, bless her heart, saw that it could be made a lot more visible and a lot more exciting were it connected to an event. That event was the National Association of Jazz Educators convention, or conference. So she had it connected to that. Having said that, what is disturbing is that if one – the award now…
The Medal of Arts was what I thought you did.
